hook_text: Mandela once said: I am not a saint. What did he mean?
clip_script: Robben Island. A former prisoner shows a Grade 4 class the tiny cell. He tells them: Mandela could not go to his own mother's funeral, or his son's. Some people called him a hero. The government of the time called him a terrorist. Later, some of his own friends were angry when he talked with the people who had jailed him. He said, I am not a saint, unless you think of a saint as a sinner who keeps on trying. Good leaders face hard choices, are not always popular, and are never perfect.
visual_style: Whiteboard prison cell with a small window, then a balance scale: on one side praise, on the other criticism, with the word human in the middle.
pacing: The cell, the cost, the critics, then the quote about trying.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and think about a hard choice a leader you know has had to make.
